messages:
alex: getting 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/responses from our frontend. I pasted the dashboard key into the Authorization header and it started failing ~10m ago.

mira_support: @alex sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl or snippet (obfuscate the key) so we can repro quickly? also which deployment: hosted / dedicated / private?

alex: hosted. here's what I ran locally:
```bash
curl -X POST 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -H \"Authorization: ApiKey sk-live_abcdef1234567890\" 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses 
  -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```

mira_support: ahh — that's the issue. Our API expects `Authorization: Bearer <key>` for dashboard/service keys (or `x-api-key: <key>` for some SDKs). `Authorization: ApiKey ...` will be rejected with 401. Can you switch header and retry?

alex: ok switching header now... still getting 401 though. same body: \"{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\"}\"

ryan_oncall: @alex quick check: are you certain that key is a hosted API key and not a dedicated/cluster-bound key? Those are scope-limited and will throw 401 when used against the hosted endpoint.

alex: created it in dashboard -> API keys -> service key. panel shows \"Hosted\" (I think).

gina: two common gotchas to try: 1) trailing newline/whitespace on the key (copy/paste) 2) wrong header scheme (mira mentioned). Can you do `printf '%s' \"$KEY\" | hexdump -C` and paste output so we can confirm hidden bytes?

alex: ran hexdump on mac (obfuscated key):
```
00000000  73 6b 2d 6c 69 76 65 5f  61 62 63 64 65 66 31 32  |sk-live_abcdef12|
00000010  33 34 35 36 37 38 39 30  0a                       |34567890.|
00000019
```

mira_support: yep there's a trailing 0a (newline) in the paste — that will produce a different token value server-side and cause `invalid_api_key` / `malformed secret`. Trim it and retry (`KEY=$(printf '%s' \"$KEY\" | tr -d '\\n')`).

alex: trimmed and re-ran with `Authorization: Bearer sk-live_abcdef123456789034567890` -> success, 200 and a response token stream. :tada:

mira_support: great! For posterity: two distinct 401 causes we saw here: wrong auth scheme (`Authorization: ApiKey`) -> 401 invalid_api_key with prefix-not-recognized message in logs; and trailing-whitespace/newline in pasted key -> 401 malformed secret / signature mismatch. We'll add a small FAQ blurb.

ryan_oncall: adding note to oncall playbook: check header scheme and hexdump for hidden bytes.

deploy-bot: Incident log auto-generated: support/6171712345 - resolved (root cause: trailing newline + wrong header scheme) :white_check_mark:

mira_support: closing thread unless you see recurrence, @alex. feel free to reopen if anything else pops up.

alex: all good, thanks everyone!
